blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Effective social interaction requires more than fluent responses: agents must reach plans that fit the participants' needs and circumstances. Existing evaluations of social agents mainly rely on LLM judges that rate the conversation, without checking the resulting plan. We introduce HICO-Bench, a benchmark of 180 everyday coordination scenarios, such as resource allocation, scheduling, and authorization, in which two agents with private information converse and then independently record the plan they agreed on. A program checks Feasibility (the two records match and satisfy both participants' private conditions), and an LLM judge checks Integrity (the conversation supports the recorded plan); passing both is a Verified Success. Each scenario has two versions that share the same public context but differ in one private condition, so the correct plan differs between them. Across thirteen LLMs, 36% of conversations rated highly for goal completion fail Verified Success. To learn from outcomes that arrive only at the end of a conversation, we propose Paired-Credit Policy Optimization (PaCPO). After each turn, PaCPO asks the agent for a tentative plan, checks it in both versions of the scenario, and rewards the turns after which the tentative plans fit their respective versions. PaCPO raises Qwen3-8B's Verified Success from 20.4% to 28.3%.
blocks.zh: 有效的社会互动需要的不仅仅是流利的反应:行为者必须制定符合参与者需求和情况的计划。 对社会代理人的现有评价主要依靠对谈话进行评分的LLM法官,而不检查由此产生的计划. 我们引入了HICO-Bench,这是180个日常协调方案的基准,如资源分配、时间安排和授权,其中两个有私人资料的代理人相互交替,然后独立记录他们同意的计划。 一个程序检查可行性(两个记录匹配并满足两个参与者的私人条件),一个LLM法官检查诚信(谈话支持记录的计划);通过这两个程序都是验证成功. 每个场景都有两种版本,相同公共背景,但在一个私人条件上有所不同,因此它们之间的正确计划不同. 在13个法学硕士中,36%的谈话被高评为目标完成不及格。 为了从对话结束时取得的成果中吸取教训,我们提议优化Paired-Credit政策。 每次转会后,PaCPO请代理商提出一个暂定计划,在两种版本的假想中检查,并奖励暂定计划符合各自版本的转会. PaCPO将Qune3-8B的验证成功率从20.4%提高到28.3%.

conversation. SOTOPIA ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) uses an LLM judge to rate
agents on goal completion, believability, and related dimensions, and
subsequent work trains agents to improve these ratings ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2025 ) . Such ratings do not verify

everyday coordination, where the decisive facts must be elicited through

blocks.en:
We introduce HICO-Bench (Hidden Information and Checkable Outcomes), a
benchmark that evaluates social interaction by its outcome. After each
conversation, both agents independently record
the agreed plan in a structured form. A program checks Feasibility : whether the two records match and satisfy all private
conditions. An LLM judge checks Integrity : whether the
conversation supports the recorded plan, for example without invented
authority or a record that contradicts what was said. An interaction is
a Verified Success only if it passes both checks. Each scenario
has two versions, or worlds , that differ in a single private
condition (e.g., whether Maya can attend) and admit disjoint sets of
correct plans; an agent that responds identically in both worlds
therefore fails at least one. Across thirteen LLMs, 36% of conversations
with Goal ≥ 8 / 10 \geq 8/10 fail Verified Success.

blocks.en:
Verified outcomes can also serve as a training signal, but they arrive
only after the final turn, leaving the contribution of individual turns
unclear. We propose Paired-Credit Policy Optimization (PaCPO),
which uses the paired worlds for credit assignment. After each turn, we
probe the agent, outside the conversation, for a tentative plan it would
record at that point, and check this plan in both worlds. Before
Leo learns whether Maya can attend, his tentative plan is the same in
both worlds and can fit at most one; once she answers, the plan formed
in each world should fit that world but not its counterpart. PaCPO
rewards the turns at which this occurs, redistributing the terminal
reward without changing each conversation’s total return. On Qwen3-8B,
PaCPO improves Verified Success from 20.4% to 28.3%, compared with
25.0% for PPO and 26.3% for GRPO trained on the same number of
dialogues. Our contributions are as follows:

blocks.en:
Within broader research on agent reasoning and interaction ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2025a ; Wang & Liu, 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) ,
Social IQa and FANToM test social commonsense and who knows what in a
conversation ( Sap et al., 2019 ; Kim et al., 2023 ) .
SOTOPIA evaluates agents in role-played social scenarios, with an LLM
judge rating goal completion, believability, and other dimensions ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) ; SOTOPIA-ToM extends this setting to information
seeking and privacy ( YS et al., 2026 ) .
Multimodal work also studies truthfulness and deception ( Kang et al., 2025b ; Kang et al., 2025a ) , personality judgments ( Kang et al., 2026 ) , and speaker alignment ( Ouyang et al., 2026a ) , alongside interactive digital humans ( Cai et al., 2025 ) and controllable multi-person video generation ( Ouyang et al., 2026b ) .
HICO-Bench focuses on the plan reached through dialogue: whether it fits
both participants’ private conditions and is supported by what they said.
We retain SOTOPIA’s ratings as complementary measures of conversation quality.

When feedback arrives only at the end of an episode, a learner must
estimate which earlier steps deserve credit. Process supervision labels each reasoning
step ( Lightman et al., 2024 ) ; VinePPO estimates a step’s value by
sampling continuations from it ( Kazemnejad et al., 2025 ) ; GiGPO and
GraphGPO compare steps that share the same state across rollouts ( Feng et al., 2025 ; Cheng et al., 2026 ) . For social agents, SOTOPIA-RL
and SAVOIR distribute LLM-judge ratings over the utterances of a
conversation ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Feng et al., 2026 ) . In free-form
dialogue, however, identical states rarely recur across rollouts, and
LLM ratings are noisy. PaCPO instead compares tentative plans across
the two worlds of a scenario and checks them with rules, so that each
comparison is verifiable.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
Effective social interaction should be judged not only by the
conversation but also by the plan it produces. HICO-Bench evaluates this
with paired scenarios and two checks, Feasibility and Integrity, whose
conjunction defines Verified Success. Across thirteen LLMs, high
conversation ratings often accompany plans that fail these checks.
PaCPO uses the paired worlds to turn end-of-conversation outcomes into
turn-level credit, improving Verified Success over the base model and RL
baselines. These results suggest that verified outcomes complement
conversation ratings, both for evaluation and as a training signal. The
benchmark currently covers six coordination families with structured
outcomes, and Integrity relies on an LLM judge; extending verification
to less structured interactions and expanding human validation are
important next steps (Appendices L and K ).

blocks.en:
Both worlds of a scenario are sampled under the same behavior-policy version.
The two trajectories are not forced to have identical language or identical length.
After each turn of the tested role, PaCPO generates one tentative plan from the visible prefix. Tentative plans at matching turn indices are checked in both worlds. When one conversation lacks a corresponding turn or a valid tentative plan, the paired credit is zero, while within-world feasibility remains available.

blocks.en: An anchor key hashes the exact actor-input token sequence together with a flag distinguishing dialogue turns from final records. It therefore contains the actor’s role card, public instructions, and full visible history. Matching is restricted to the same scenario, world, and role. We disable approximate string matching and semantic state merging; partner-private fields and verifier state are not added to the key. This keeps decision-relevant history intact while making shared anchors depend on identical visible prefixes.

blocks.en: GraphGPO builds a directed graph separately for each rollout group. Nodes are the same exact-history anchors, and unit-weight edges connect successive actor steps. A dialogue with R = 1 R=1 connects to a shared success node; other terminal nodes remain trajectory-specific. The released routine computes shortest-path distances to success. With distance normalization disabled, the step score is 10 ​ ( 0.10 ) D ⁡ ( s t + 1 ) 10(0.10)^{D(s_{t+1})} , where D D is the successor’s distance to success. Unreachable nodes receive the upstream fallback distance, one greater than the largest finite distance. blocks.en: We evaluate task-specific training in two settings: database-grounded recommendation and bilateral negotiation. Table 4 reports their results.

blocks.en: We select hotel and restaurant goals from MultiWOZ 2.2 dialogue-state annotations ( Zang et al., 2020 ) and use the corresponding MultiWOZ 2.1 entity databases ( Eric et al., 2020 ) . Each source contributes one domain-specific recommendation task with explicit user constraints, such as area, price range, cuisine, or hotel amenities. We select goals with a database match and omit booking requests and requests for a preselected named entity. Train, development, and test retain their original source splits; repeated constraint profiles are removed across splits.
blocks.zh: 我们从MultiWOZ 2.2对话状态说明(Zang等,2020年)中选择旅馆和餐馆目标,并使用相应的MultiWOZ 2.1实体数据库(Eric等,2020年)。 每一来源都提供一项针对具体领域的建议任务,并有明确的用户限制,如面积、价格范围、烹调或旅馆设施。 我们选择与数据库匹配的目标,并省略预选的指定实体的预订请求和请求。 Train, Development,并测试保留了原源分解;重复的制约剖面被从分解中去掉.

blocks.en: Each pair retains the public request and database while changing one private user constraint. Both worlds have valid recommendations, and their valid entity sets are disjoint. The visitor holds the requirements privately; the assistant asks questions, searches the database, and recommends one entity by name. A successful episode requires that the selected entity satisfy every private constraint and be unambiguously identified in the final message. This constraint communication endpoint tests whether elicited requirements reach the actual recommendation. The test set contains 77 paired scenarios and 154 dialogues.
blocks.zh: 每对都保留公开请求和数据库,同时改变一个私人用户限制. 两个世界都有有效的建议,其有效的实体集是脱节的. 访客私下持有这些要求;助理提问,搜索数据库,推荐一个实体的名字。 一个成功的插曲要求被选定的实体满足每一个私人限制,并在最后信息中明确指明。 这种制约性通信终点测试是否得出了实际建议。 测试集包含77个对偶情景和154个对话框.

blocks.en: We retain CaSiNo’s campsite setting ( Chawla et al., 2021 ) , with three units each of food, water, and firewood. Each participant has private high-, medium-, and low-priority items, valued at 5, 4, and 3 points per unit, together with reasons for those preferences. To construct paired worlds, we keep the tested participant’s card fixed and replace the partner’s complete preference-and-reason card with one from the same original split. This changes which allocations benefit the partner while retaining the public negotiation setting.
blocks.zh: 我们保留了CaSiNo的营地(Chawla等人,2021年),每个营地有三套食物、水和木柴。 每位参加者都有私人高、中和低优先项目,每股价值为5、4和3分,以及这些偏好的原因。 为了构建对等的世界,我们保留被测试的参与者的卡片固定下来,并用相同的原始分出卡片来取而代之。 这种改变使合作伙伴受益,同时保留公开谈判的环境。

blocks.en: The participants negotiate a complete allocation that both accept. We report agreement rate and normalized Nash surplus, based on the Nash bargaining product ( Nash, 1950 ) . We take the product of both participants’ nonnegative utility gains above the five-point walk-away value and divide it by the maximum attainable product in that world. Episodes without agreement receive zero surplus. These measures distinguish reaching an agreement from finding a mutually beneficial allocation. The test set contains 43 paired scenarios and 86 dialogues.
blocks.zh: 与会者就双方接受的全额分配进行谈判。 我们根据纳什讨价还价计划(Nash, 1950年), 我们把两位参与者的非负作用收益的产物放在五分远去的价值之上,并用世界上能达到的最大产物加以分化。 未经同意的集会获得零盈余. 这些措施将达成协议与找到互利的分配区分开来。 该测试集包含43个对偶情景和86个对话框.

blocks.en: A task position identifies a scenario, world, and tested role. The eligible pool is the intersection of positions with an available frozen Integrity request for Base, PPO, PaCPO, and GRPO ( G = 4 G=4 ): 239 positions. We stratify by the six interaction families, sort family names and then task keys lexicographically, and shuffle each family’s keys using one Python random-number generator initialized with seed 20260924. Selecting the first ten keys per family without replacement yields 60 shared positions spanning 43 scenarios. Selection uses task identifiers and family labels, not Feasibility or Integrity scores, and is fixed before Kimi-K3 is queried. We reuse each method’s output at these same positions without regenerating dialogues, giving 60 evaluations per method and 240 in total. Identical requests are scored once and reused, producing 203 unique Kimi-K3 requests; reported statistics give equal weight to all 240 model–task evaluations.

Two expert annotators review 48 dialogues from Base and PaCPO,

blocks.en: HICO-Bench covers six coordination families whose arrangements can be represented as structured records and checked against explicit conditions. This supports reproducible feasibility tests, but does not cover the full range of social interaction, such as emotional support or relationships without a well-defined final outcome. Extending the benchmark requires identifying verifiable outcomes without reducing these interactions to inappropriate formal objectives. Feasibility success is feasibility under the specified conditions, not a general judgment of social appropriateness.
blocks.zh: HICO-Bench包括六个协调家庭,其安排可以作为结构化记录,并根据明确的条件加以检查。 这支持可再生的可行性测试,但并不包括全方位的社会互动,如情感支持或没有明确最终结果的关系. 扩大基准要求确定可核查的成果,而不要将这些互动减少到不适当的正式目标。 可行性成功是在规定条件下的可行性,而不是对社会适当性的一般判断。
